heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Polymaker PolyLite ABS out of the box with its fully enclosed chamber, hardened steel nozzle, and high bed temperature capability. Tuned for an 18 mm³/s max volumetric flow rate, the printer safely achieves speeds up to 214 mm/s while maintaining excellent layer adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 18 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap outer walls and infill speeds within the safe 214 mm/s limit.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan completely (set to 0%) to prevent localized draft chilling and corner warping.
Set the chamber exhaust fan to 0% during printing and enable a 10-15 minute bed preheat at 100°C to saturate the enclosure above 45°C.
Configure Part Cooling Fan threshold: Min 10% / Max 25% with 30s layer time thresholds, and enable 'Keep fan always on' to stabilize thermal mass.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and print warping off the bed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Chamber ambient temperature is too low or cold drafts from the aux fan triggered thermal contraction stresses.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the aux fan, preheat the bed to 100°C for 15 minutes before printing to heat-soak the chamber to >45°C, and use a 5mm outer brim with 0.1mm gap.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer cracking and delamination along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or excessive volumetric flow leading to poor polymer melt fusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce maximum part cooling fan speed to 20%, ensure nozzle temp is at 255°C, and limit max volumetric speed to 18 mm³/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Bubbling surface finish and stringing artifacts
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyLite ABS has absorbed atmospheric moisture causing steam micro-explosions at the nozzle exit.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours in a dedicated filament dryer or the X1C chamber, and print directly from an airtight dry box or Bambu AMS with desiccant.

faq.question: Can I leave the Bambu Lab X1C glass door open when printing PolyLite ABS?
faq.answer: No. Keep both the front glass door and top glass lid fully closed to trap heat and prevent ambient drafts, which will immediately warp ABS parts.

faq.question: Is the Bambu AMS compatible with Polymaker PolyLite ABS?
faq.answer: Yes, PolyLite ABS spools fit and feed seamlessly through the AMS, provided the spool is not physically damaged and desiccant packs inside are fresh.

faq.question: Why use glue stick on a textured PEI plate for ABS?
faq.answer: PolyLite ABS adheres extremely strongly to PEI; the glue stick acts as a release interface to prevent the print from tearing the PEI coating off the steel plate during removal.

faq.question: What is the optimal chamber preheat routine for this setup?
faq.answer: Home the toolhead, raise the bed near the top glass, set the bed temperature to 100°C, and allow 10 to 15 minutes of soak time until the internal chamber reads at least 45°C.
